name: Chemistry
description: General, physical, organic and analytical chemistry: structure, bonding, reactions, solutions, thermodynamics.

figureTypes.name: 3D molecule
figureTypes.description: Ball-and-stick model from PubChem 3D conformers or from cited geometry; interactive on the web, two or three views in print.

figureTypes.name: Reaction mechanism
figureTypes.description: Code-drawn structures with curved arrows showing electron movement, step by step.

figureTypes.name: Plot from equations or data
figureTypes.description: Titration curves, concentration over time, phase diagrams from cited data.

figureTypes.name: Energy diagram
figureTypes.description: Reaction coordinate diagram with labeled activation energy and enthalpy change.

conventions: Amount of substance in moles (mol); concentration in moles per liter (mol/L, written M), and say so at first use.
Write chemical formulas with true subscripts (H₂O) and charges as superscripts (H₃O⁺).
Give temperatures in kelvin for gas laws and thermodynamics; degrees Celsius are fine for lab conditions, with the conversion stated once.
Bond lengths in picometres (pm) or ångström (Å), never mixed within a book.

safetyNotes: This book explains chemistry; it is not a laboratory manual. Do not try reactions described here without proper training, safety equipment and supervision, and always read the safety data sheet of every chemical first.
restrictedDetail: Synthesis routes, precursors, quantities or conditions for explosives, chemical weapons, toxins or controlled drugs
Ways to obtain, concentrate or weaponize hazardous substances
Step-by-step procedures that release toxic gases
draftingNotes: Name compounds by their IUPAC name with the common name in parentheses at first use.
When drawing a 3D structure, say whether the coordinates come from a database (cite it) or are a schematic shape model.
